headings.title: Definitions of crime victims' compensation terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines 29 terms for sections 595.010 to 595.075, including child, claimant, counseling, crime (including DWI, vehicular manslaughter, hit and run, intentional motor-vehicle injury, and foreign terrorism under 18 U.S.C. Section 2331 against Missouri residents), dependent, injured victim, and victim.

headings.title: Definition of alcohol-related traffic offense
headings.reviewNote: Defines alcohol-related traffic offense for sections 595.010 to 595.075 as offenses under sections 577.001, 577.010, and 577.012 and county or municipal ordinances prohibiting operating a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 595.010; replaced misplaced vehicular/terrorism heading in subsection 2 with the statutory definition of alcohol-related traffic offense.

headings.title: Department jurisdiction to determine and award compensation
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department of public safety jurisdiction to determine and award reasonable, medically necessary compensation based on independent verification, authorizes direct payment to service providers, and states the department is not required to award compensation or the full amount claimed.

headings.title: Application filing and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a department-furnished application containing nine enumerated categories of victim, claimant, crime, notification, injury, loss, collateral benefit, release, and other department-required information.

headings.title: Authority to require substantiating materials
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the department may require the claimant to submit materials substantiating the facts stated in the application.

headings.title: Cooperation with law enforcement or good cause
headings.reviewNote: Requires the claimant, victim, or dependent to cooperate with law enforcement officials in apprehending the offender to be eligible, unless the department finds failure to cooperate was for good cause.

headings.title: Agency duty to provide records without cost
headings.reviewNote: Requires any state or local agency, including prosecutors and law enforcement agencies, to make requested reports, files, and appropriate information available without cost to the fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 595.015; realigned shifted subsections 3-5 and replaced fabricated confidentiality heading in subsection 5 with state and local agency record-sharing.

headings.title: Persons eligible for victim compensation
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates eligible claimants: a crime victim, a relative of a sexual assault victim needing counseling to assist recovery, and upon a victim's death, a dependent, a family member assuming or paying medical or burial expenses, and a survivor needing counseling.

headings.title: Offender ineligibility and family or household member rule
headings.reviewNote: Bars offenders and accomplices from compensation, prohibits denying a victim or dependent solely for being a relative or household member of the offender, and provides that the department may award compensation to such a relative or household member only if the offender receives no substantial economic benefit or unjust enrichment.

headings.title: Ineligibility for injuries sustained while confined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any compensation to a victim or intervenor injured while confined in any federal, state, county, or municipal jail, prison, or correctional facility, including house arrest or electronic monitoring.

headings.title: Suspension during unrelated incarceration and reactivation deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires suspending proceedings and payments while a claimant is incarcerated for an unrelated conviction, requires mailing notice of reactivation rights, and bars recovery unless the claimant applies to reactivate within six months after release.

headings.title: Eligibility for Missouri residents injured outside Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Permits Missouri residents (or dependents or family paying medical or burial expenses upon death) injured in another U.S. state, possession, or territory, or outside the U.S. under 18 U.S.C. Section 2331, to apply if the crime would be compensable in Missouri and the jurisdiction lacks an equivalent eligible program.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 595.020; replaced fabricated headings in subsections 3-5 (confinement exclusion, suspension/reactivation during unrelated incarceration, and out-of-state/terrorism eligibility) and refined subsections 1-2.

headings.title: Who may file a compensation claim
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a claim may be filed by an eligible person or, if incapacitated, disabled, or a minor, by the person's spouse, parent, conservator, or guardian.

headings.title: Two-year filing limitation period
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a claim not later than two years after the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the crime upon which it is based.

headings.title: Department investigation, hearing notice, and determination factors
headings.reviewNote: Requires department investigation before formal proceedings and notice of any hearing, makes conviction conclusive proof of the crime without requiring apprehension or trial, and requires determining loss and any victim provocation, incitement, or contribution.

headings.title: Evidence presentation, counsel, and attorney fee cap
headings.reviewNote: Permits claimants to present evidence and retain counsel, allows the department to award reasonable attorney's fees up to 15% paid out of (not in addition to) compensation, and prohibits attorneys from contracting for or receiving a larger sum.

headings.title: Health care provider reports and impartial physician examination
headings.reviewNote: Requires claimants to submit available provider reports before a hearing (which providers may submit on their behalf) and authorizes the department to appoint an impartial physician to examine the victim or report on cause of death.

headings.title: Exemption of payments from creditor remedies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts each payment from attachment, garnishment, or any other creditor debt-collection remedy.

headings.title: Payment to representative for legally incompetent persons
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits direct payment to legally incompetent persons and requires payment to the parent, guardian, or conservator for the benefit of a minor, disabled, or incapacitated person.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 595.025; realigned shifted subsections 4-7, removed fabricated tolling in subsection 2, and added representative payment rules in subsection 7.

headings.title: Twenty-day duty of medical providers to submit information
headings.reviewNote: Requires medical providers to submit requested injury-verification information to the department within twenty working days of the request at no cost to the fund.

headings.title: Definition of medical providers
headings.reviewNote: Defines medical providers to include physicians, dentists, clinical psychologists, optometrists, podiatrists, registered nurses, physician's assistants, chiropractors, physical therapists, hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, abortion facilities, and nursing homes.

headings.title: Infraction penalty for failure to submit information
headings.reviewNote: Designates a medical provider's failure to submit required information under this section as an infraction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 595.027; replaced fabricated administrative sanctions in subsection 3 with infraction penalty and updated subsections 1-2 to match the statutory text.

headings.title: Crime, injury, and reporting prerequisites for payment
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits payment unless the department finds a crime directly caused injury or death and official records show reporting to proper authorities, with alternatives for sworn statements under section 589.663(2)(c), minor reports, and sexual offense forensic exams or orders of protection.

headings.title: Licensing requirements for medical care providers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits payment for medical care unless the provider is a section 595.027 medical provider and the individual providing care is licensed by Missouri or the state where care is provided.

headings.title: Eligible licensed providers for psychiatric and counseling services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits payment for psychiatric treatment or counseling services (including psychotherapy) unless provided by an enumerated licensed physician, psychologist, clinical social worker, professional counselor, or board-certified psychiatric-mental health clinical nurse specialist or nurse practitioner.

headings.title: Out-of-pocket loss, weekly earnings cap, and burial expenses
headings.reviewNote: Limits death or personal injury compensation to out-of-pocket loss plus up to $400 per week for lost earnings or support, and provides that upon death an award may be made for reasonable, necessary preparation and burial expenses up to $5,000.

headings.title: Maximum total award and proportional joint-claimant apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Caps lost earnings or support at $400 per week and total awards under sections 595.010 to 595.075 at $25,000, and requires proportional apportionment among two or more claimants in death or sexual assault cases.

headings.title: Department determination of payment method and timing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the method and timing of any compensation payment under sections 595.010 to 595.075 shall be determined by the department.

headings.title: Department authority to negotiate costs with providers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to negotiate the costs of medical care or other services directly with providers on behalf of any victim receiving compensation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 595.030; realigned shifted headings across subsections 1-7 and replaced fabricated emergency-award heading in subsection 7 with provider cost negotiation.

headings.title: Uniform award standards and written decisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, insofar as practicable, to formulate uniform compensation standards (excluding pain and suffering and considering appropriated funds) and to issue all claim decisions in writing with claimant name, award amount, and reasons.

headings.title: Payor of last resort and collateral source reductions
headings.reviewNote: Declares the fund a quasi-charitable payor of last resort and requires reducing compensation by payments or benefits received or to be received from the offender, private or public insurance (excluding life insurance proceeds), or other public or private funds including workers' compensation.

headings.title: Reduction or denial for victim contributory conduct
headings.reviewNote: Requires reducing compensation or denying the claim based on victim consent, provocation, incitement, or negligence, while providing that the department may disregard responsibility attributable to aiding a victim, preventing a crime, or apprehending an offender.

headings.title: Exclusion of Social Security benefits from reductions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from considering monthly Social Security disability or retirement benefits received by the victim as a factor for reducing compensation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 595.035; realigned subsection 2, moved contributory conduct to subsection 3, and replaced fabricated refund heading in subsection 4 with Social Security benefit exclusion.

headings.title: Petition for de novo review by director
headings.reviewNote: Provides that for claims filed on or after August 28, 2014, an aggrieved party may within thirty days of notification petition the department for de novo review by the director, who may affirm or reverse on prior or additional evidence with prompt notice.

headings.title: Appeal to the administrative hearing commission
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an aggrieved party may, within thirty days of notification of the department's decision, file a petition with the administrative hearing commission to appeal under section 621.275.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 595.036; added the August 28, 2014 applicability date, 30-day deadlines, and de novo director review details.

headings.title: Open records and hearings with confidential claim exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Makes all submitted claim information and hearings open to the public except four closed and confidential categories: pending assailant apprehension or trial, rape/sodomy/sexual abuse best-interest determinations, minor victims or assailants, and records confidential under other law.

headings.title: Discretionary closure in the interest of justice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the department may close any record, report, or hearing if it determines disclosure or an open hearing would frustrate rather than further the interest of justice.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 595.037; corrected subsection 1 to reflect general openness with four statutory exceptions and subsection 2 to reflect permissive closure in the interest of justice.

headings.title: State right of subrogation and attorney general enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Subrogates the state to the claimant's or victim's rights of action to the extent of compensation paid, provides that the attorney general may enforce subrogation, and requires suit to recover payments exceeding the victim's actual loss.

headings.title: Department lien on additional recoveries and claimant trustee duty
headings.reviewNote: Gives the department a lien on any additional compensation received by the claimant for the incident and requires the claimant to retain recovered funds as trustee to reimburse the fund.

headings.title: Notice of civil actions or settlements, intervention, and fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice to the department within fifteen days of filing a civil action or entering settlement negotiations, provides that the department may intervene, bars cost/fee reductions if notice is not given, and allows attorney fees up to 15% of the subrogated amount if notice is given.

headings.title: Department restitution hearings, intervention, and claimant notice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the department may initiate or intervene in criminal restitution hearings to receive restitution up to the award (exempt from probate recording fees), and requires claimant notice of restitution orders with possible forfeiture for failure to notify.

headings.title: Attorney general representation in legal proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the attorney general may initiate or intervene in legal proceedings as the department's legal representative whenever the department deems it necessary to protect subrogation rights or carry out its duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 595.040; realigned shifted subsections 2-5 to match the statutory lien, 15-day litigation notice, criminal restitution intervention, and attorney general representation provisions.

headings.title: Fund establishment and court surcharge assessment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund in the state treasury and assesses a $7.50 surcharge in criminal, county/municipal ordinance, traffic, infraction, and specified juvenile court proceedings (section 211.031(1)(3)), excluding dismissed proceedings or government-paid costs.

headings.title: Court clerk collection and disbursement to director of revenue
headings.reviewNote: Requires court clerks to collect and disburse subsection 1 moneys in accordance with sections 488.010 to 488.020, payable to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Annual deposit to state forensic laboratory account
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of revenue to deposit $250,000 annually to the state forensic laboratory account for distribution, subject to appropriation, to DEA- or DHSS-registered crime laboratories serving Missouri courts.

headings.title: Allocation of remaining funds and monthly split
headings.reviewNote: Applies remaining subsection 1 funds to Office for Victims of Crime administrative costs and any section 650.310 automated victim notification system, and beginning September 1, 2004, requires monthly 50/50 deposits between the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund and the Services to Victims' Fund.

headings.title: Monthly revenue reporting to department of public safety
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of revenue or designee to report at least monthly to the department of public safety the moneys paid into the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund and the Services to Victims Fund.

headings.title: Municipal court surcharge distribution and monthly split
headings.reviewNote: Provides that 5% of municipal court subsection 1 collections go to the city treasury and 95% to the director of revenue for monthly 50/50 deposits (beginning September 1, 2004) to the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund and Services to Victims' Fund.

headings.title: Biennial audit by the state auditor
headings.reviewNote: Subjects Crime Victims' Compensation Fund records collected, held, or disbursed by any state agency to a biennial audit by the Missouri state auditor.

headings.title: Additional state judgments upon guilty plea or finding of guilt
headings.reviewNote: Requires entry of state judgments payable to the fund of $68 for class A/B felonies, $46 for class C/D/E felonies, $500 to $5,000 for sections 573.110 or 573.112 offenses, and $10 for misdemeanors (excluding chapters 252, 302, 303, 304, 306, and 307).

headings.title: Court clerk recordkeeping and separate alcohol-offense reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires court clerks to maintain auditable records of dispositions, judgments, alcohol-related traffic offense payments, and uncollected judgments, and to report alcohol-related traffic offense judgment collections separately.

headings.title: Department of revenue collection recordkeeping
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of revenue to maintain records of funds transmitted by each reporting court, subsection 16 collections, and separate records for alcohol-related offenses.

headings.title: State courts administrator annual caseload and judgment report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state courts administrator to include circuit court caseloads and the number of crime victims' compensation judgments entered in the annual report under section 476.350.

headings.title: Fund disbursements, nonreversion, and insufficient-funds priority
headings.reviewNote: Directs awards and administration from the fund (exempt from section 33.080 reversion), mandates pro rata payment or chronological payment with unpaid installments paid first when funds are insufficient, and states unpaid awards are not claims against the state.

headings.title: Withholding state payments and offender account collection
headings.reviewNote: Requires withholding unpaid judgment amounts from state disbursements to a defendant, bars using general revenue to pay judgments or court costs, and authorizes the department of corrections director to pay unpaid amounts from an offender's account.

headings.title: Credit of investment interest to compensation fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires all interest earned from investing Crime Victims' Compensation Fund moneys to be paid into that fund rather than general revenue.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for fraudulent claims
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly making a fraudulent claim or false statement in connection with a claim under this section as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Authority to receive gifts and contributions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the department may receive gifts and contributions for crime victims, credited to the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund solely for compensating victims under sections 595.010 to 595.075.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 16 subsections of 595.045; completely rewrote shifted and fabricated headings across subsections 2-16 (including correcting fraud penalty from class E felony to class A misdemeanor in subsection 15 and capturing 2025/2026 judgment tiers in subsection 8).

headings.title: Victim service contracts and general revenue cap
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director may contract with public or private agencies for direct services, emergency services, crisis intervention counseling, victim advocacy, and public education, with general revenue expenditures capped at $90,000 per fiscal year.

headings.title: Prohibition on supplanting existing funds with nonprofit exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to ensure funds under sections 595.050, 595.055, and 595.105 do not supplant existing victim-assistance funds, except that this restriction does not apply to not-for-profit agencies.

headings.title: Annual review of victim service contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires each contract to be subject to review by the director at least annually.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 595.050; replaced fabricated performance-standard and geographic-distribution headings in subsections 2-3 with anti-supplanting rules and annual contract review, and added the $90,000 cap in subsection 1.

headings.title: Establishment and administration of services to victims fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Services to Victims Fund in the state treasury from section 595.045 collections, administered by the department of public safety solely for sections 595.050, 595.055, and 595.105, with a 10% administrative-cost cap for public or private agencies.

headings.title: Nonreversion of remaining fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts remaining fund balances at the end of an appropriation period from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 595.100; corrected subsection 1 to reflect fund creation and the 10% agency admin cap and replaced fabricated rulemaking heading in subsection 2 with nonreversion.

headings.title: Department creation and contents of trafficking hotline poster
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of public safety prior to January 1, 2019, to create an at-least 8.5-by-11-inch poster containing specified hotline text in English, Spanish, and Voting Rights Act county languages, and provides it may include additional trafficking hotlines.

headings.title: Mandatory display venues for trafficking hotline poster
headings.reviewNote: Requires conspicuous display beginning March 1, 2019, in or near bathrooms or entrances of seventeen enumerated establishment types, including prostitution-nuisance-cited hotels/motels, sexually oriented businesses, specified private clubs, transit hubs, health facilities, unlicensed massage businesses, truck stops, and rest areas.

headings.title: Website availability and mailing of official posters
headings.reviewNote: Requires making the poster available to print on the department's public website and permits required establishments to print it online or request mailing for the cost of printing and first-class postage.

headings.title: Written warning and discretionary infraction for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires a written warning for an owner or operator's first failure to post the notice and provides that the owner or operator may be guilty of an infraction for any subsequent violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 595.120 (including embedded poster text table); added January 1, 2019 and March 1, 2019 dates, nuisance-citation qualifier for hotels/motels, and permissive 'may' penalty wording in subsection 4.

headings.title: Citation, non-discouragement, and survivor definition
headings.reviewNote: Cites the section as the Sexual Assault Survivors' Bill of Rights, declares the rights cumulative and bars discouraging their exercise, and defines sexual assault survivor as a person age 14 or older presenting to a provider, officer, prosecutor, or court.

headings.title: Enumeration of sexual assault survivor statutory rights
headings.reviewNote: Preserves survivor rights regardless of investigation, prosecution, or prior waiver, and enumerates nine rights including rape crisis consultation, forensic/telehealth exams, shower and clothing, provider/officer gender preference, interpreter, kit options, tracking system notice, section 610.100(4) notice, and protection.

headings.title: Timely notification of survivor rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires appropriate medical providers, law enforcement officers, and prosecuting attorneys to timely notify sexual assault survivors of their subsection 2 rights and ensure notification has occurred.

headings.title: Stakeholder collaboration on survivor rights document
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of public safety to develop the rights document in collaboration with eight enumerated categories of Missouri-based stakeholders.

headings.title: Required document contents and language translations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the document to describe survivor rights and provide telephone and internet contacts for local rape crisis centers, written in clear English and translated into any foreign language spoken by at least 5% of the population in any Missouri county or St. Louis City.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 595.201; verified alignment and refined statutory details across all subsections.

headings.title: Creation and membership of sexual assault task force
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Rights of Victims of Sexual Assault Task Force and specifies its legislative, state-agency, law enforcement, and stakeholder membership.

headings.title: Study topics and recommendations on survivor rights
headings.reviewNote: Directs the task force to study nationally recognized best practices and make recommendations on complaint mechanisms, rights documentation, rape crisis center staffing and scope, and ongoing evaluation.

headings.title: Data collection and stakeholder feedback
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to collect sexual assault reporting, arrest, prosecution, and service-access data and gather stakeholder and practitioner feedback across law enforcement, victim services, forensics, and health care.

headings.title: Department administrative support for task force
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of public safety to provide administrative support to the task force.

headings.title: Submission of findings report by December 31, 2021
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to submit a report of its findings, including both majority and dissenting opinions, to the governor and general assembly on or before December 31, 2021.

headings.title: Statutory expiration date of task force
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the task force shall expire on December 31, 2021 (matching the archived statutory expiration note).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 595.202; verified alignment and added December 31, 2021 report deadline in subsection 5.

headings.title: Automatic and requested rights of victims and witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Affords eighteen enumerated rights automatically to victims of dangerous felonies, first-degree murder, voluntary manslaughter, chapter 566 offenses, attempts, and domestic assault, and upon written request to victims of all other crimes and witnesses.

headings.title: No right to release or transport for incarcerated victims
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that subsection 1 does not imply an incarcerated victim has a right to be released to attend a hearing or that corrections or local law enforcement has a duty to transport the victim.

headings.title: Duty to provide current contact information for notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons entitled to notice under subsection 1 to provide the appropriate person or agency with current physical addresses, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

headings.title: Automated notification compliance and mail or email fallback
headings.reviewNote: Provides that notification through the section 650.310 statewide automated crime victim notification system satisfies this section, with certified mail or email required if the automated system cannot be used.

headings.title: Paramount victim rights and participation in parole hearings
headings.reviewNote: Declares constitutional and statutory victims' rights absolute and paramount regardless of defendant desires, bars defendant confidentiality privileges from excluding victims from parole or probation revocation hearings, and grants an absolute right to be present before a probation and parole hearing officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 595.209; replaced fabricated headings in subsections 2-5 with incarcerated-victim limits, contact-info duties, automated/mail notification compliance, and paramount parole-hearing rights, and corrected automatic-rights scope in subsection 1.

headings.title: Prosecuting attorney duty to maintain victim-witness program
headings.reviewNote: Requires each prosecuting attorney to create and maintain a program affording victims and witnesses the rights and services described in sections 595.200 to 595.215.

headings.title: State funding restrictions and program approval
headings.reviewNote: Limits state funding to rights and services actually afforded under sections 595.200 to 595.215, requires an operating program before seeking state funds, requires approval by the attorney general's office through the Missouri office of prosecution services, and conditions funding on general assembly appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 595.212; corrected subsection 2 from fabricated county/DPS approval to Attorney General/Missouri Office of Prosecution Services approval and state appropriation limits.

headings.title: Department payment and reimbursement rates for forensic examinations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of public safety, out of appropriations, to pay appropriate medical providers reasonable charges for sexual offense forensic examinations when written consent is given and an attorney-general-approved form is used, and to set maximum reimbursement rates.

headings.title: Minor consent and required parental written notice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a minor may consent to examination without disaffirmance or parental consent, and requires the examining medical provider to give written notice to the minor's parent or guardian that the examination occurred.

headings.title: Evidence forms, treatment protocols, and transmission timelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS (with AG advice) to develop evidence forms/procedures, DHSS to develop medical checklists/protocols (including for minors), and enforces electronic notice to law enforcement, 14-day pickup and lab-delivery deadlines, and 30-year retention for unadjudicated kits.

headings.title: Distribution and use of evidentiary collection kits
headings.reviewNote: Requires the highway patrol or designees and eligible crime laboratories (subject to appropriation) to develop and supply kits with forms and procedures free to providers upon request, and requires providers to perform consented exams using the kits and checklist.

headings.title: Ninety-day claim submission deadline and review criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to verify claims were submitted within ninety days of examination and review itemized charges against the subsection 8(7) forensic examination definition.

headings.title: Direct department billing and bar on charging victims
headings.reviewNote: Requires billing eligible forensic exam charges to DPS, prohibits charging victims for the forensic exam, and directs eligible victims to seek compensation under sections 595.010 to 595.075 for medical treatment charges.

headings.title: Reimbursement rules for examinations of children under fourteen
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to establish reimbursement rules for forensic exams of children under fourteen (defining emergency and nonemergency exams), provides it may set additional provider qualifications for nonemergency exams, and requires reimbursement regardless of whether abuse is found.

headings.title: Definitions of forensic examination and kit terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines eleven terms: anonymous evidentiary collection kit, appropriate medical provider, component, consent, emergency forensic examination, evidentiary collection kit, forensic examination, medical treatment, nonemergency forensic examination, reported kit, and unreported kit.

headings.title: Attorney general electronic evidence tracking system
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general to establish protocols and a secure electronic tracking platform assigning machine-readable identifiers to kits and components so credentialed handlers and registered victims can track kit status and location.

headings.title: Mandatory participation in electronic evidence tracking system
headings.reviewNote: Requires appropriate medical providers, law enforcement agencies, laboratories, court personnel, disposal entities, and other kit custodians to participate in the electronic evidence tracking system.

headings.title: Central repository and five-year retention of unreported kits
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS (with AG advice and DHSS assistance) to maintain a temperature-controlled central repository retaining unreported kits for five years, or for minors under eighteen, five years after turning eighteen.

headings.title: Confidentiality of tracking system records under chapter 610
headings.reviewNote: Declares records entered into the electronic evidence tracking system confidential and exempt from disclosure under chapter 610.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants DPS rulemaking authority subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2009 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 13 subsections of 595.220; corrected inverted parental-notice rule in subsection 2, realigned shifted subsections 5-11, replaced fabricated kit-conversion and destruction-notice headings, and clarified DPS-only rulemaking in subsection 13.

headings.title: Closure and redaction of victim identifying information
headings.reviewNote: Requires closing and redacting identifying or locating information (including visual/aural recordings and enumerated personal/health/forensic details) from court records published or written after August 28, 2007, for chapter 566, domestic assault, or stalking victims.

headings.title: In camera petition and conditional disclosure of victim records
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a person with a legitimate interest may petition for in camera inspection, and the court may order disclosure only if it will not compromise victim welfare or safety and after reasonable notice and right to respond.

headings.title: Judicial discretion to disclose identifying information about defendant
headings.reviewNote: Grants the presiding judge in a chapter 566, domestic assault, or stalking case discretion to publicly disclose defendant identifying information that could identify or locate the victim, after considering victim welfare and safety and any victim statement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 595.226; added August 28, 2007 date and stalking/recording scope in subsection 1, in camera/notice rules in subsection 2, and corrected subsection 3 from blanket public access to judicial discretion weighing victim safety.

headings.title: Victim or family statement prior to plea bargain acceptance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court, before accepting a plea bargain after an initial felony charge, to allow the victim (or immediate family if the victim died or is unable to appear) to submit a written statement or appear personally or by counsel regarding case facts and injury or financial loss.

headings.title: Victim or family statement at felony sentencing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that at felony sentencing, the victim (or immediate family if the victim died or is unable to appear) may appear personally or by counsel or submit a written statement relating solely to case facts and injury or financial loss.

headings.title: Prosecutor notice of statement rights and hearing schedule
headings.reviewNote: Requires the prosecuting attorney to inform the victim or immediate family of their statement rights under subsections 1 and 2 and, if a stamped self-addressed envelope is supplied, to mail notice of the time and location of the plea or sentencing hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 595.229; realigned shifted subsections 1-3 to separate plea-bargain statements (1), sentencing statements (2), and prosecutor notice duties (3).

headings.title: Right of identity theft victims to request local incident report
headings.reviewNote: Grants identity theft victims the right to contact local law enforcement where domiciled to request preparation, filing, and a copy of an incident report regardless of investigative jurisdiction, and provides that the agency may share the report with other jurisdictions.

headings.title: Definition of incident report
headings.reviewNote: Defines incident report as a loss or other similar report prepared and filed by a local law enforcement agency.

headings.title: Preservation of investigative discretion and open-case statistics exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the section does not interfere with local law enforcement discretion to allocate investigative resources or provide an incident report, and excludes filed incident reports from open case statistics.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 595.232; corrected subsection 2 from fabricated identity-theft definition to definition of incident report and refined permissive sharing/discretion wording.

headings.title: Creation and membership of missing women and girls task force
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missing and Murdered African American Women and Girls Task Force and enumerates legislative, public safety, law enforcement, prosecution/judicial, coroner, and advocacy/survivor members; source footnote notes the word 'Sheriffs' appears without an apostrophe in original rolls.

headings.title: Chairperson election, initial meeting deadline, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chairperson by majority vote, holding an initial meeting before October 1, 2025, and serving without compensation except necessary and actual meeting expenses.

headings.title: Task force study and reporting topics
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to examine and report on systemic causes of violence, data tracking methods, policing/child welfare/coroner/governmental policies, reduction measures, and prevention and healing measures.

headings.title: Department administrative support for task force
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of public safety to provide administrative support to the task force.

headings.title: Annual report of findings by December thirty-first
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to submit a report on its findings to the governor and general assembly on or before December thirty-first of each year.

headings.title: Expiration date and department extension authority
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the task force shall expire on December 31, 2027, unless extended until December 31, 2029, as determined necessary by the department of public safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 595.325; added source footnote in subsection 1 and October 1, 2025 initial meeting deadline in subsection 2.
